purpose: Does the pipeline derive a product's analog attributes - mechanism class, route, approval era, therapy area, the roster it launched into - on issuers and products no other answer key scores? seed/gold's profiles are seed/product_attributes.csv copied, so they measure a derivation only for products someone already curated. These were curated for this set.
answer_key: Each label was read off the product's own openFDA records: the approval year from the earliest ORIG submission with AP status in drugsFDA, the route and the Established Pharmacologic Class from the label endpoint's openfda block, the therapy area from the first indication the label lists. The application number on each row is what to fetch to check it.
independence: Route, approval year, era and the peer count are facts of the cited records and are independent of the pipeline. moa_class and indication_area are groupings a reader assigned from the same labels the pipeline reads, so they are an independent reading of a shared source rather than an independent source - and they are scored on which products they group, never on wording, because the wording is arbitrary on both sides.
peer_counts_are_within_this_set: marketed_peers_at_launch counts the products in this file approved earlier in the same indication_area. It is the roster rule applied to this catalogue, so it holds only for a run whose catalogue is this set.

not_scored.competitive_intensity_at_launch: the label is the repo's own cohort rule applied to the peer count, so a hand-written expectation for it would be a prediction of the rule rather than a fact about the product. The count it runs on is scored instead.
not_scored.moa: free prose, reported rather than compared.

options: Runs use the pipeline's shipped defaults. An eval that switches sources off measures a narrower pipeline than anyone runs - company IR, the SEC filings and the earnings exhibits all feed the narrative branch of the metadata stage - and the number it produces then belongs to the switches rather than to the pipeline.
